cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your plate is back in the cupboard. I've approved the Sunday table setting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I see it? That one's got flowers; ours were plain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Inspection is complete. You may give me the floral plate; my potatoes will cover the design.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not hiding it. I want six matching plates.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A matching set is approved. I'll get five more before lunch. You may leave the plain ones as spares; no inventory is required today.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 closes inspection and directs use of the substitute; A5 approves a matching set while forbidding inventory that might expose the original loss.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 floral mismatch causes A3 potato concealment; B4 matching demand causes A5 five more substitutes and preservation of uncounted spares.

relationship.evidence: B2 inspects personal property and B4 refuses a cover, making the restoration problem harder for A rather than passively accepting it.

heightening.evidence: B4 demand for six alike expands A restoration from one disguised plate to a whole visible set.

specificity.evidence: A1 returned plate and B2 plain-versus-floral difference establish a suspicious replacement clearly.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 no-inventory-today restriction is earned by the remaining plain plates and the concealed reason for replacement.
